excerpts: Dak lights up Tennessee.** Another week, and another high-flying day for the Cowboys quarterback. [Dak Prescott](https://www.nfl.com/players/dak-prescott) was in a flow state all afternoon, completing 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns, and adding a rushing score of his own for good measure. He had plenty of time to throw and open receivers to target throughout the contest, leading a Dallas offense that seemed to score 51 points with the utmost ease. [CeeDee Lamb](https://www.nfl.com/players/ceedee-lamb) recorded yet another 10-plus-catch, 100-plus-yard outing (11 for 132 and a touchdown), [George Pickens](https://www.nfl.com/players/george-pickens) tacked on seven grabs (including [a fantastic, toe-tapping grab](https://www.nfl.com/videos/can-t-miss-play-pickens-pirouettes-for-toe-tap-catch-and-30-yard-gain-against-titans) to set up a score) for 102 yards and a touchdown, and the Cowboys cruised against a Titans defense that was guaranteed to give up big plays. We didn't learn anything new about this group Sunday, we were just reminded of the potential to put up big numbers against inferior competition. **Titans descend back to reality.** Tennessee has been the most entertaining one-win team in recent memory over the last few weeks, taking the Browns and Bengals to the wire and battling with the Jaguars before falling to its AFC South rival by double digits. The Titans could credit their offense and quarterback [Cam Ward](https://www.nfl.com/players/cam-ward) for this stretch of competitive football, but it ended Sunday with a harsh reminder of how bad this defense currently is. With [Jeffery Simmons](https://www.nfl.com/players/jeffery-simmons) now playing in Chicago and [Amani Hooker](https://www.nfl.com/players/amani-hooker) wearing a Bills uniform, the Titans no longer had a couple of playmakers capable of covering up for mistakes and deficiencies elsewhere, and boy, did it show on Sunday. Dallas racked up 480 yards of offense, converted 4 of 6 third downs and got basically whatever it wanted offensively all afternoon. The fact the Cowboys only reached third down six times in a game in which they ran 63 plays is telling in itself. This unit needs work and likely won't improve much for the remainder of this campaign.

excerpts: **Pettine will be a topic of conversation this week.** It began before Mike Pettine officially took over as play-caller, but after his shift into leading defensive chair this week, the veteran coach's name will remain in the news cycle thanks in large part to a Cowboys pass rush that is finding consistent success. The unit got after Cam Ward all afternoon Sunday, sacking him five times and generating a 41.7% pressure rate. [Quinnen Williams](https://www.nfl.com/players/quinnen-williams) and [James Houston](https://www.nfl.com/players/james-houston) led the way, with each registering five pressures and two sacks, continuing an upward trend that began when Pettine arrived as a senior defensive assistant. The rest of the unit's relative success against Tennessee -- the Titans finished 3 for 10 on third down, turned it over once and lost time of possession by nearly six minutes -- as well as the 21-point scoring difference will throw Pettine's name into topic bars across sports media this week as if he has suddenly saved this defense. Sunday's performance should be handled with caution, though. The Titans still allowed Tony Pollard to run for 110 yards, gave up 346 yards of offense and still surrendered 30 points. It will take much more (against a better team) to convince anyone that a play-caller change was all this embattled defense needed. But one development can be properly credited to Pettine: The pass-rushing unit -- especially Williams -- has certainly found its teeth. **Next Gen Stats Insight for [Titans-Cowboys](https://pro.nfl.com/games/game/ab99929a-4feb-11f1-abca-2c54536568a9) (via NFL Pro):** Quinnen Williams generated five pressures and two sacks across 18 pass rushes in Week 11 against the Titans (27.8% pressure rate), including a strip-sack fumble of Cam Ward in the red zone on a play late in the fourth quarter.

recap.paragraph: In Dallas, the Cowboys and Titans battled for a win. Dallas scored on its first 8 possessions and won 51-30! Dak Prescott tossed 4 touchdown passes and ran for another. Cam Ward zipped a 59-yard touchdown pass to Carnell Tate. Then Quinnen Williams gave Dallas more momentum with a strip-sack! Dallas ran the fumble back 70 yards. The win put the Cowboys at 5-6, while the Titans fell to 1-9.
